_partNote: Every class here is nominally an antenna or a sensor, so each prompt is pinned to a different shape class rather than a different detail: an upright flat rectangular array panel (1), a sphere (2), a ring of thin vertical rods on a disc (3), one tall narrow cylinder (4), a low horizontal disc of concentric rings (5), a flat triangular slab (6), and a dome-tipped cone (7). Navigation and guidance are effects rather than objects, so 5, 6 and 7 draw the hardware that identifies them — a choke-ring antenna, a ring laser gyro block, a seeker nose section — with no satellites, no signal lines and no trajectories.

partPrompts.1: A flat rectangular radar array panel standing upright with a slight backward tilt on a low wedge mount: a thick rectangular slab whose entire front face is covered by a coarse regular grid of about five by four small square radiating elements, with a plain frame around the edge. Flat and rectangular, not a dish and not a drum; no mast, no vehicle, no rotation and no beam.
partPrompts.2: A gimballed electro-optical ball turret hanging from a short cylindrical mounting neck: a smooth sphere with one flat facet on its front carrying two round window apertures of different sizes side by side, and a seam ring running around the sphere where it rotates. One rounded compact object, no aircraft, no wings, no antennas and no beam.
partPrompts.3: A circular direction-finding antenna array: a round flat ground-plane disc lying horizontally with eight thin vertical rod antennas standing evenly spaced around its rim and one slightly taller rod at the center. Thin bare verticals on a plain disc, no dish, no panel, no lattice tower, no cables and no building.
partPrompts.4: An expendable sonobuoy canister standing upright on its end: one tall narrow cylinder roughly seven times taller than it is wide, with a flat lid on top, two shallow bands running around the body, and a plain rounded bottom. A single plain tall cylinder, nothing deployed from it, no antenna, no cable, no hydrophone and no water.
partPrompts.5: A choke-ring satellite-navigation antenna seen three-quarter: a squat cylindrical housing whose flat top face is a bullseye of four concentric raised rings around one small central element, with a short connector stub under the base. A low ringed disc, not a dish and not a flat panel; no mast, no tripod, no satellites and no signal lines.
partPrompts.6: A ring laser gyro block sitting flat on a plain surface: one solid equilateral triangular slab, chunky and thick, with a small round mirror mount fitted at each of its three corners and plain flat faces between them. A triangle, clearly not a box and not a disc; one object, no wiring, no circuit board, no housing and no light paths drawn.
partPrompts.7: The nose section of a missile standing upright, its plain flat cut end resting on the surface: a short tapering conical body topped by a smooth glassy hemispherical dome, with a fine joint line where the dome meets the cone. Only the front section, closed and solid at the back rather than a cutaway; no fins, no fuselage, no whole missile, no target and no flight path.
